Nonlinear operating-point optimization belongs to the selected autopilot cohort.
theory.delta: Every actual XML fin map/limits is bound independently, including single-product two-axis layouts and passive fins excluded from command authority. No provider alias or invented unique mechanism replaces these model data.
theory.state: The named C++ allocator validates/passes normalized virtual channels. Actual mixer gains and per-fin limit state reside in the generated JSBSim FCS; it is not a second client-side allocator. Passive rolleron patches have zero virtual-channel authority.
theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.
theory.uncertainty: Shared mixer schema has different actual gains, fin identities, zero authority, asymmetry and limits per model. Empty descriptor parameter_refs does not mean parameter-free: card, source TOML and actual serialized XML hashes are mandatory.

Nonlinear operating-point optimization belongs to the selected autopilot cohort.
theory.delta: Every actual XML fin map/limits is bound independently, including single-product two-axis layouts and passive fins excluded from command authority. No provider alias or invented unique mechanism replaces these model data.
theory.state: The named C++ allocator validates/passes normalized virtual channels. Actual mixer gains and per-fin limit state reside in the generated JSBSim FCS; it is not a second client-side allocator. Passive rolleron patches have zero virtual-channel authority.
theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.
theory.uncertainty: Shared mixer schema has different actual gains, fin identities, zero authority, asymmetry and limits per model. Empty descriptor parameter_refs does not mean parameter-free: card, source TOML and actual serialized XML hashes are mandatory.

theory.delta: Every actual XML fin map/limits is bound independently, including single-product two-axis layouts and passive fins excluded from command authority. No provider alias or invented unique mechanism replaces these model data.
theory.state: The named C++ allocator validates/passes normalized virtual channels. Actual mixer gains and per-fin limit state reside in the generated JSBSim FCS; it is not a second client-side allocator. Passive rolleron patches have zero virtual-channel authority.
theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.
theory.uncertainty: Shared mixer schema has different actual gains, fin identities, zero authority, asymmetry and limits per model. Empty descriptor parameter_refs does not mean parameter-free: card, source TOML and actual serialized XML hashes are mandatory.

theory.state: The named C++ allocator validates/passes normalized virtual channels. Actual mixer gains and per-fin limit state reside in the generated JSBSim FCS; it is not a second client-side allocator. Passive rolleron patches have zero virtual-channel authority.
theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.
theory.uncertainty: Shared mixer schema has different actual gains, fin identities, zero authority, asymmetry and limits per model. Empty descriptor parameter_refs does not mean parameter-free: card, source TOML and actual serialized XML hashes are mandatory.

theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.

theory.state: The named C++ allocator validates/passes normalized virtual channels. Actual mixer gains and per-fin limit state reside in the generated JSBSim FCS; it is not a second client-side allocator. Passive rolleron patches have zero virtual-channel authority.
theory.io: Three normalized channels -> asymmetric native scale -> finite channel actuator -> per-fin authored gain sum -> physical-fin rate/stops -> aerodynamic table input. Exact generated XML coefficients and identities are authoritative.
theory.discretization: FCS evaluates channel scale/actuator before fin-demand expressions in document order; physical fin travel is limited per native substep. The C++ wrapper does not reproduce or bypass this simulation.
theory.uncertainty: Shared mixer schema has different actual gains, fin identities, zero authority, asymmetry and limits per model. Empty descriptor parameter_refs does not mean parameter-free: card, source TOML and actual serialized XML hashes are mandatory.
